2026:UHC:9323
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.794 of 2026
Gurbhajan Singh ... Revisionist.
Versus
Harminder Kaur ... Respondent.
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, learned counsel for the revisionist.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J. (Oral)
By means of the present Criminal Revision, the
revisionist has sought setting-aside of the order dated
12.08.2026, passed by learned Additional Principal
Judge, Family Court, Vikasnagar, Dehradun in Misc.
Criminal Case No. 58 of 2025, Harminder Kaur vs.
Gurbhajan Singh, whereby the learned Court has fixed
interim maintenance of Rs.10,000 per month with effect
from the date of application, payable on or before the 10th
day each succeeding month in favor of Smt. Harminder
Kaur/respondent.
2. Assailing the impugned order dated
12.08.2026, passed by Additional Principal Judge,
Family Court, Vikasnagar District, Dehradun, learned
counsel for the revisionist/husband would submit that
the learned Additional Principal Judge, Family Court,
Vikasnagar, District Dehradun has erred by granting an
interim maintenance of ₹10,000 per month to the wife.
Learned counsel for the revisionist assails the impugned
order dated 12.08.2026 on the ground that the amount
which has been taken into consideration by the learned
Additional Judge, Family Court, Vikasnagar, District
1

UKHC010181982026
2026:UHC:9323
Dehradun to draw the inference that the monthly
income of the revisionist/husband is ₹30,000 per month
includes the amount of sale deed and he would submit
that the monthly income of the husband/revisionist is far
below ₹30,000 per month.
3. The next ground being agitated on behalf of
the learned counsel for the revisionist is that, in addition
to the responsibility of maintaining the wife, there are
two ailing brothers of the revisionist whose responsibility
of maintenance and medication, etc., has also fallen on
the revisionist.
4. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that without any reasonable cause, the
wife/respondent has left the company of the
husband/revisionist, and as such, there is no question of
granting any interim maintenance to the
wife/respondent. He would further submit that the
wife/respondent has initiated multiple litigations, and
the application for maintenance has been filed after the
institution of the suit for divorce, after she left the
matrimonial home at her own volition.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the
revisionist, what falls for consideration in this Criminal
Revision is whether the learned Additional Judge, Family
Court, Vikasnagar, District Dehradun has erred by
drawing the inference that the revisionist/husband is
having a monthly income of Rs.30,000/-?
6. A perusal of the impugned order in para 9
would reveal that there have been multiple bank
transactions in the bank account of the revisionist, and
on the basis of the same, the learned Additional Judge,
Family Court, Vikasnagar, District Dehradun has drawn
2

UKHC010181982026
2026:UHC:9323
an inference that on account of the bank transactions of
the revisionist/husband, a monthly income of ₹30,000 is
being deemed to be his income. Learned counsel for the
revisionist, however, does not deny that the respondent
is the wife of the revisionist.
7. The second ground agitated on behalf of the
revisionist that the maintenance application has been
filed after the institution of the divorce. This cannot be a
ground to deny interim maintenance to the respondent
wife.
8. The next ground being agitated that the
respondent wife is living separately from the husband
since the last two years also cannot be a ground to deny
interim maintenance.
9. The other ground being agitated on behalf of
the learned counsel for the revisionist is that the learned
Additional Judge, Family Court, Vikasnagar, District
Dehradun has not dealt with the aspect of the matter
that the respondent wife has left the matrimonial house
on her own volition.
10. All these aspects which are being raised by the
learned counsel for the husband/revisionist would find
deliberation in the final outcome of the maintenance
proceedings. At this stage, the only consideration at the
stage of granting interim maintenance is the relationship
between the parties and the income of the husband.
11. In the present case, the monthly income of the
husband has been assessed by the learned Additional
Judge, Family Court, Vikasnagar, District Dehradun on
the basis of the bank transactions. Hence, this finding is
based on record and does not warrant any interference. It
3

UKHC010181982026
2026:UHC:9323
is not denied by the learned counsel for the revisionist
that the respondent is the wife of the revisionist.
12. In such view of the matter, there is no scope
for interference at this stage.
13. Hence, the Criminal Revision lacks merit and
the same is dismissed accordingly. However, the
revisionist would be at liberty to raise all defences
available to him and the maintenance application will be
decided on its own merit without being influenced by any
observation made in this order.
14. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of
accordingly.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.)
13.10.2026
Shiv/
